title: Hadith Knowledge
description: General User → Pro. Familiar hadith examples, broader meanings and short everyday applications requiring deeper understanding. Covers intention, sound guidance, balance in worship, knowledge, trust, companionship and common misreadings. All questions are Pro level within the General User audience; specialist terminology, grading disputes and reference-number memorization are excluded.
levelMethod: Pro describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires deeper understanding, connecting familiar teachings and distinguishing common misconceptions beyond Mid, without specialist study. This is General User Pro, not the separate Ultra bank. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Which example illustrates the teaching about intentions in the opening hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari?

options.text: Migration motivated by a worldly gain
Trading with an unclear price
Planting food eaten by birds
Settling an argument through witnesses

questions.explanation: The report uses migration for worldly aims to show that an outward act and its intended purpose must be distinguished.

questions.question: In the hadith about doubtful matters, what does grazing near a protected pasture illustrate?

options.text: Every unfamiliar thing is forbidden
Approaching a boundary risks crossing it
Public approval makes something lawful
Avoiding all trade is necessary

questions.explanation: The comparison warns about moving close to forbidden conduct through doubtful matters; it does not declare every unfamiliar thing forbidden.

questions.question: What does the hadith about rejected actions make central to an act of worship?

options.text: The number of participants
The expense of organizing it
Accord with the Prophet’s guidance
The admiration it receives

questions.explanation: The report makes conformity to prophetic guidance essential. Popularity and expense cannot establish a religious practice.

questions.question: Which example accompanies the command for excellence in all things in the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws?

options.text: Choosing the largest possible sacrifice
Giving every animal a special name
Restricting kindness to useful animals
Reducing an animal’s suffering during slaughter

questions.explanation: The report applies excellence even to slaughter, showing that lawful action still requires humane care.

questions.question: Which comparison did the Prophet use when advising Ibn Umar about life in this world?

options.text: A stranger or passing traveler
A merchant owning every market
A ruler with permanent authority
A guest guaranteed a long stay

questions.explanation: The comparison presents worldly life as temporary, encouraging preparation rather than attachment as though it will last forever.

questions.question: What qualification accompanies the preference for a strong believer over a weak believer?

options.text: Only the strong receive any reward
Both believers have good in them
Weak believers should stop trying
Strength means wealth alone

questions.explanation: The report preserves the goodness of both while encouraging beneficial effort. Preference does not mean that the weaker believer has no worth.

questions.question: How does the hadith about recording deeds describe a good deed sincerely intended but not performed?

options.text: It is always recorded as a sin
It earns reward only if announced
A complete good deed is recorded
It cancels every earlier obligation

questions.explanation: The report describes Allah’s generosity in recording a sincere good intention even when the deed is not carried out.

questions.question: Which pair is presented as worthy of aspiration in the hadith about two admirable examples?

options.text: Inherited wealth and a famous family
Long life and public popularity
Physical strength and military victory
Rightly used wealth and practiced, taught wisdom

questions.explanation: The examples concern using gifts well: spending wealth rightly and applying and teaching wisdom, rather than simply possessing advantages.

questions.question: What did Umm Sulaym’s question to the Prophet demonstrate about learning purification?

options.text: A personal religious question can be asked respectfully
Personal questions must always remain unanswered
Only men may ask about purification
Modesty requires guessing every ruling

questions.explanation: She asked about a sensitive purification matter and received an answer. Respectful learning can coexist with modesty.

questions.question: Which three qualities are joined in the hadith about wealth, honor and being raised by Allah?

options.text: Wealth, authority and popularity
Charity, forgiveness and humility
Silence, isolation and celibacy
Travel, trade and physical strength

questions.explanation: The report links charity with wealth, forgiveness with honor, and humility before Allah with being raised in status.

questions.question: Whose eating from a Muslim’s planting is described as charity for the planter?

options.text: Only the planter’s own family
Only people who request permission
People, birds or animals
Only travelers who cannot pay

questions.explanation: The report includes human and animal benefit, extending the charitable value of planting beyond a direct gift to a person.

questions.question: What question exposed the problem with a zakah collector’s claimed personal gifts?

options.text: Were the gifts wrapped attractively?
Did every gift have the same price?
Had he thanked each giver publicly?
Would gifts have come without his official role?

questions.explanation: The Prophet questioned whether the gifts would have reached the collector at home, separating personal generosity from benefits arising through office.

questions.question: Which image does the hadith use to teach learning from harmful experience?

options.text: Being stung again from the same hole
Losing a camel in a desert
Spilling water from a full vessel
Sailing a boat against the wind

questions.explanation: The image encourages alertness after experience, rather than repeatedly exposing oneself to the same avoidable harm.

questions.question: Which conduct is condemned through the description of a person with two faces?

options.text: Explaining truth in two languages
Presenting deceptive loyalties to different groups
Being friendly to unfamiliar people
Disagreeing politely with a friend

questions.explanation: The warning concerns deceptive dealings with different groups. Changing language or speaking courteously is not itself the condemned conduct.

questions.question: What warning accompanies the hadith’s description of religion as easy?

options.text: All religious duties become optional
Effort in worship is discouraged
Overburdening oneself leads to being overcome
Only complete perfection has value

questions.explanation: The report warns against unsustainable severity while encouraging sincere striving and hope, rather than abandoning religious practice.

questions.question: What gift does the Prophet connect with Allah intending good for someone?

options.text: Winning every discussion
Remembering the most reference numbers
Having the largest audience
Understanding the religion

questions.explanation: The praised gift is religious understanding. Fame, argument and a large store of numbers are not the measure named here.

questions.question: How does the hadith describe knowledge being taken away from the community?

options.text: Scholars die and ignorant leaders answer without knowledge
All written books disappear at once
Every learner immediately forgets all words
People stop needing guidance entirely

questions.explanation: The report links the loss of learned people with the rise of uninformed answers that mislead both speakers and listeners.

questions.question: How did the Prophet answer men proposing extreme lifelong worship routines?

options.text: He approved every increase in hardship
He described worship alongside sleep, breaking fast and marriage
He required all companions to avoid marriage
He replaced obligatory prayer with rest

questions.explanation: His own example corrected the idea that greater self-denial necessarily represents greater devotion.

questions.question: What danger does the hadith about disputing parties associate with persuasive speech?

options.text: Every eloquent person must be dishonest
A fluent claim needs no examination
A judgment may favor someone taking another’s right
A favorable decision removes all wrongdoing

questions.explanation: The warning distinguishes a decision based on presented arguments from the true entitlement known to the person making the claim.

questions.question: Which pair illustrates the influence of good and harmful companionship?

options.text: A farmer and a traveler
A teacher and a student
A host and an unexpected guest
A musk seller and someone working bellows

questions.explanation: The pleasant scent and harmful smoke illustrate how company can affect a person, rather than ranking occupations as moral identities.

questions.question: Why can two people making the same outward journey differ in its religious reward?

options.text: Their purposes can differ despite matching actions
Travel distance is the only measure
A shared destination guarantees equal reward
Other people’s praise determines the reward

questions.explanation: The migration example directs attention to purpose; identical outward movement does not establish identical intention.

questions.question: Why does the report about lawful and forbidden matters also mention the heart?

options.text: Good feelings erase forbidden boundaries
Inner soundness influences outward conduct
Physical fitness determines every ruling
Outward actions have no religious importance

questions.explanation: The report connects moral boundaries with the heart’s condition. Inner reform and outward choices belong together.

questions.question: Which reasoning conflicts with the hadith about rejected religious actions?

options.text: Religious practice needs sound guidance
A popular practice can need examination
Sincerity alone establishes any invented ritual
Good motives require a sound method

questions.explanation: A sincere motive does not by itself establish a ritual as part of the religion; conformity to guidance also matters.

questions.question: What broader principle follows from requiring humane care even in lawful slaughter?

options.text: A lawful aim excuses every method
Excellence applies only inside prayer
Animal suffering has no moral relevance
Permission does not remove responsibility for how one acts

questions.explanation: The example distinguishes an action’s permissibility from the care and excellence required in carrying it out.

questions.question: Which understanding best fits the advice to live like a passing traveler?

options.text: Let temporary life serve preparation for the Hereafter
Avoid all work and family responsibilities
Assume tomorrow is guaranteed
Treat every comfort as forbidden

questions.explanation: A traveler’s perspective changes priorities. The comparison does not itself require abandoning ordinary responsibilities or declaring comforts forbidden.

questions.question: Why is using the strong-believer hadith to ridicule someone’s weakness a poor reading?

options.text: It proves believers must never improve
It ignores the goodness affirmed in both believers
It makes every difference in ability unreal
It limits faith to athletic performance

questions.explanation: The report combines encouragement to strengthen oneself with recognition of good in the weaker believer, not contempt.

questions.question: What does rewarding an intended good deed reveal about how deeds are recorded?

options.text: Good intentions make action unnecessary
People can calculate everyone’s final reward
Allah’s generosity extends beyond completed outward acts
A wish guarantees all duties are fulfilled

questions.explanation: The report gives hope through Allah’s generous accounting. It does not turn intention into completion of an outstanding duty.

questions.question: What distinguishes the aspiration praised in the two-examples hadith from destructive envy?

options.text: Wanting every advantage taken from others
Resenting any person who teaches well
Measuring goodness only by possessions
Wanting similar goodness without another losing theirs

questions.explanation: The examples invite aspiration toward beneficial use of gifts, not resentment or a wish to deprive their recipients.

questions.question: Which claim is challenged by Umm Sulaym’s respectful question about purification?

options.text: Modesty always requires silence about necessary learning
Sensitive questions deserve respectful answers
Worship can require learning personal rulings
Questions can be asked with good manners

questions.explanation: Her example distinguishes modest conduct from allowing embarrassment to prevent necessary religious understanding.

questions.question: Which claim goes beyond the hadith that charity does not decrease wealth?

options.text: Charity carries blessing beyond simple subtraction
Every donation guarantees an immediate cash increase
Forgiveness can be a source of honor
Humility before Allah can raise someone

questions.explanation: The report encourages trust in Allah’s promise; it does not specify an immediate increase in a bank balance after each gift.

questions.question: How does the planting hadith broaden a person’s understanding of charity?

options.text: Only cash gifts have charitable value
Every profitable crop is religiously worthless
Benefit can reach others without a direct handover
Animal benefit excludes human benefit

questions.explanation: Food growing through someone’s planting can benefit others and count as charity, even without a separate personal presentation.

questions.question: Why is calling something a gift insufficient to settle the collector’s case?

options.text: All gifts between any people are forbidden
Only expensive gifts raise concerns
A private label removes public accountability
Its connection to entrusted authority still matters

questions.explanation: The report examines why the benefit arose. A favorable label does not remove a conflict with an entrusted role.

questions.question: Which distinction best fits the warning about being stung twice?

options.text: Forgiveness and sensible precautions can coexist
Forgiveness requires repeating every risk
Caution requires suspecting every person
Past harm justifies harming innocent people

questions.explanation: Learning from harm need not mean revenge or universal mistrust; sensible precautions are consistent with the report’s lesson.

questions.question: How does tact differ from the two-faced conduct condemned in the hadith?

options.text: Tact requires endorsing incompatible lies
Tact can preserve truth while adapting its delivery
Any change of tone proves deception
Friendliness always means agreeing with wrongdoing

questions.explanation: The moral issue is deception, not every adjustment in tone. Truthful courtesy need not involve dishonest loyalties.

questions.question: Which interpretation keeps both ease and striving together in the hadith?

options.text: Remove every duty that feels demanding
Make worship as exhausting as possible
Aim sincerely for sound practice without destructive excess
Stop practicing unless perfection is certain

questions.explanation: The report joins moderation with striving toward correctness, so ease is not a license to discard duties.

questions.question: Why does knowing many quotations alone not demonstrate the gift praised in the understanding hadith?

options.text: Remembering any religious wording is forbidden
Only public speakers can understand religion
Reference numbers determine a person’s sincerity
Understanding requires grasping meaning, not merely recalling words

questions.explanation: The report praises comprehension. Remembering words can help learning, but recall and understanding are not identical.

questions.question: Why are many available religious statements not enough to prevent the danger in the knowledge-loss hadith?

options.text: Statements can circulate without knowledgeable guidance
Popularity always establishes an answer’s soundness
A confident tone replaces subject knowledge
Learners should never ask anyone questions

questions.explanation: The danger is uninformed authority and misleading answers, not simply a shortage of circulating words.

questions.question: What mistake lay behind treating the Prophet’s balanced worship as insufficient?

options.text: Recognizing the value of regular prayer
Equating greater severity with greater devotion
Allowing time for ordinary human needs
Learning how the Prophet worshipped

questions.explanation: The response shows that prophetic balance is guidance, rather than a lower standard to surpass through self-imposed extremes.

questions.question: Why does a favorable judgment not make a knowingly false claim morally sound?

options.text: Winning always establishes innocence before Allah
The better speaker automatically owns the property
A decision on presented evidence cannot change the underlying right
Another person’s rights end when they speak poorly

questions.explanation: The report warns against knowingly taking another’s entitlement through persuasive presentation, even after receiving a favorable decision.

questions.question: What is the main point of the musk-and-bellows comparison?

options.text: Every musk seller has perfect character
Every metalworker is morally corrupt
Only paid lessons can influence behavior
Companionship can leave beneficial or harmful effects

questions.explanation: The occupations supply an illustration of influence. The lesson concerns companionship, not judging all workers in either trade.

questions.question: Two volunteers do identical work; one seeks Allah’s pleasure, the other only admiration. What follows from the intentions hadith?

options.text: Outward similarity does not establish equal religious reward
Both must have identical intentions
The admired volunteer necessarily receives greater reward
Their motives become irrelevant once work ends

questions.explanation: The migration example teaches that the purpose behind an outward act matters to its religious reward.

questions.question: An offer has a serious unresolved concern about permissibility. What best applies the doubtful-matters lesson?

options.text: Proceed because the profit is large
Pause and seek qualified clarification
Declare every similar offer forbidden
Ignore the concern if friends approve

questions.explanation: Caution about a genuine unresolved concern protects religious boundaries. Seeking clarification is different from declaring everything unfamiliar forbidden.

questions.question: A post invents a fixed ritual and promises a reward without evidence. What best applies the rejection hadith?

options.text: Accept it because the author means well
Require it because many people share it
Check its religious basis before treating it as prescribed
Assume attractive wording establishes its reward

questions.explanation: The report calls for conformity to guidance; an appealing purpose or presentation does not establish a prescribed ritual or promised reward.

questions.question: An animal handler says a lawful task excuses avoidable roughness. Which reply best fits the excellence hadith?

options.text: Kindness matters only when people watch
A useful result excuses all suffering
Excellence applies only to expensive animals
Lawfulness still requires care in the method

questions.explanation: The report’s animal example directly challenges careless methods in a lawful task. Excellence includes reducing avoidable suffering.

questions.question: A person repeatedly postpones repentance because life feels permanent. Which response fits the traveler comparison?

options.text: Act on needed change while the opportunity exists
Wait until retirement to consider accountability
Treat present opportunities as guaranteed forever
Abandon every family duty immediately

questions.explanation: The temporary-life perspective encourages timely preparation. It does not guarantee another opportunity or require neglecting responsibilities.

questions.question: Someone mocks a struggling believer as worthless using the strength hadith. What important wording should correct them?

options.text: The report denies any value in effort
The report affirms good in both believers
The report equates strength only with muscle
The report forbids seeking beneficial improvement

questions.explanation: Encouragement toward strength should be read alongside the report’s recognition of goodness in the weaker believer.

questions.question: A sincere plan to visit a sick neighbor is prevented by an unexpected illness. What hope fits the recording-deeds hadith?

options.text: The prevented visit must count as wrongdoing
Only an announced intention can earn reward
Allah can reward the sincere good intention
The intention removes every future responsibility

questions.explanation: The report gives hope of reward for genuinely intending good even when it is not carried out.

questions.question: A friend teaches beneficial knowledge well. Which response fits the admirable-examples hadith?

options.text: Hope the friend loses that ability
Treat teaching as worthless without fame
Compete to hide useful knowledge from learners
Wish to learn and benefit others similarly

questions.explanation: The praised aspiration concerns practicing and sharing wisdom, rather than resenting the person who has been given it.

questions.question: A learner is embarrassed to ask about a needed purification ruling. What best follows Umm Sulaym’s example?

options.text: Ask a knowledgeable teacher respectfully and privately if needed
Keep guessing to prove personal modesty
Assume the ruling does not apply
Replace learning with unverified comments

questions.explanation: Her example supports respectful questions about necessary religious matters. Embarrassment need not leave a learner without guidance.

questions.question: After donating, someone sees a lower account balance and says the hadith failed. What is the soundest correction?

options.text: Every donation must return cash that day
The hadith does not promise an instant cash replacement
A donation only counts when it earns profit
Bank records determine whether Allah rewards charity

questions.explanation: Allah’s promise should not be reduced to a specified banking outcome. The report gives no deadline for an immediate cash return.

questions.question: Birds eat fruit from a Muslim gardener’s tree. How does the planting hadith frame this benefit?

options.text: Only purchased bird food can count
It removes the need for all other duties
It can count as charity for the planter
It is worthless without a human recipient

questions.explanation: The report expressly includes birds benefiting from planting. Such charity does not by itself replace separate religious obligations.

questions.question: A buyer offers a charity’s purchasing officer a private reward for choosing their supplier. Which question applies the collector’s lesson?

options.text: Is the reward small enough to hide?
Can it be renamed a friendship token?
Will accepting it improve personal popularity?
Would this benefit be offered without the entrusted role?

questions.explanation: The scenario applies the report’s test of benefits arising through office. A personal label does not resolve the trust concern.

questions.question: A person deceived by the same seller is offered an identical unchecked deal. What fits the repeated-sting lesson?

options.text: Use the experience to verify and take precautions
Repeat the deal to demonstrate forgiveness
Assume every other seller is dishonest
Seek revenge on the seller’s relatives

questions.explanation: The lesson supports learning from experience and avoiding a repeated trap, without extending blame to uninvolved people.

questions.question: Someone privately tells two rival groups false stories, claiming exclusive loyalty to each. Which teaching most directly addresses this?

options.text: The encouragement to plant beneficial crops
The warning against two-faced dealings
The reward for an intended good deed
The comparison of life to a journey

questions.explanation: The deception changes with the audience and fuels conflicting loyalties, illustrating the two-faced conduct condemned in the report.

questions.question: A learner says religion’s ease means abandoning duties whenever inconvenient. Which correction fits the hadith?

options.text: Ease makes every religious duty optional
Only exhausting practice has religious value
Ease accompanies sincere practice and avoiding excess
One mistake means all effort should stop

questions.explanation: The same report that mentions ease encourages striving and warns against overburdening oneself, rather than removing religious commitment.

questions.question: A student knows a quotation but asks how its meaning applies. How does the understanding hadith frame this effort?

options.text: As proof that memorization has no value
As a reason to stop asking questions
As something reserved for famous speakers
As seeking comprehension beyond memorization

questions.explanation: The report praises understanding religion. Asking for explanation can help move from remembering wording toward grasping its meaning.

questions.question: A popular speaker confidently answers every religious question without studying it. Which danger from the knowledge-loss hadith is relevant?

options.text: Uninformed answers can mislead speaker and audience
Confidence is sufficient evidence of knowledge
A large audience guarantees sound guidance
Any answer is better than admitting uncertainty

questions.explanation: The report warns about people answering without knowledge and misleading others. Public confidence does not supply the missing learning.

questions.question: Someone calls lifelong rejection of sleep and marriage a superior religious path. What best applies the three-men report?

options.text: Approve every hardship as greater devotion
Follow prophetic balance rather than inventing superior severity
Treat all voluntary worship as unnecessary
Make celibacy a requirement for every believer

questions.explanation: The Prophet corrected extreme proposals by explaining his own balanced life. The report challenges making such severity a superior religious ideal.

questions.question: A person knowingly wins another’s property through a misleading presentation. What principle applies despite the favorable decision?

options.text: The successful presentation makes the taking honest
The other party’s weak speech cancels their right
The decision does not make knowingly taking it rightful
A favorable decision removes accountability before Allah

questions.explanation: The report warns that persuasive success cannot turn knowingly taking another person’s right into a morally rightful act.

questions.question: A group repeatedly normalizes ridicule, and a member notices copying it. Which lesson fits the companionship comparison?

options.text: Influence exists only during planned lessons
Joining a group removes personal responsibility
Every member’s occupation determines their character
Repeated company can shape conduct without formal teaching

questions.explanation: The comparison draws attention to effects of company. Noticing a harmful influence is a reason to reconsider participation and habits.
